close_reason: Decision record landed at JmapBackend::principal_id doc — explicit cross-reference to bd:JMAP-jfia.13 plus 'this suggestion is wrong' framing for the structural enforcement of the no-JIT-lookup policy.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:936-939 — JmapBackend::principal_id is declared with signature:

  fn principal_id(caller: &Self::CallerCtx) -> Option<&jmap_types::Id> { ... }

No &self receiver. A future contributor (or AI tool) will see this as "an oversight, surely the backend wants self access to its identity store" and suggest changing to `fn principal_id(&self, caller: ...) -> ...`. That suggestion is WRONG.

Why no &self is correct (the doc at backend.rs:919-935 makes the argument; this decision-record makes it visible at review time):

  - Backends MUST NOT mint identity. Identity is the HTTP layer's job. The JMAP layer only READS the result of authentication.
  - Without &self, a backend physically cannot do a JIT lookup against its storage. The auth-layer middleware must pre-resolve and stash the principal Id inside CallerCtx BEFORE dispatch() runs.
  - The function-vs-method distinction is the structural enforcement of the policy. Comments alone could be ignored; the type system makes the wrong thing impossible.
  - Consumers that want JIT-resolved identity (e.g. database-backed JWT → principal mapping) wire that mapping into the HTTP layer's CallerCtx construction step.

A consumer hitting "I can't access self.users.lookup() inside principal_id" should restructure their HTTP layer to do the lookup before dispatch — not lobby for a &self signature change here.

Defending this shape protects the workspace identity-seam policy from drift. Worth a permanent decision record so future reviewers do not re-litigate.
title: principal_id as associated function (no &self) structurally enforces 'no JIT identity lookup'
